title: A survey of textual cyber abuse detection using cutting-edge language models and large language models

bias_targets.methodology: Conducting a systematic literature review to evaluate how recent cyber abuse detection studies address skewed dataset distributions through specific evaluation metrics (e.g., weighted F1-score) and pre-processing techniques (e.g., SMOTE, data augmentation, undersampling).
Surveying and analyzing existing research that utilizes large language models and traditional machine learning to detect sexism, misogyny, and gender-based hate speech in social media text.
Reviewing literature on the performance of transformer-based architectures and neural networks in detecting racist and xenophobic cyber abuse across multiple languages.
Identifying and summarizing studies that focus on the automated classification and detection of homophobic hate speech using multi-lingual language models.
